root_cause_label: Misread FastText.py Source — Fixated on Deprecated API Stubs Instead of np.array(copy=False) Bug in predict()
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent read FastText.py in step 8, saw the buggy np.array(probs, copy=False) call in predict() but ignored it, instead fixating on deprecated cbow/skipgram stubs as the root cause, and never tested the predict() path that triggers the NumPy 2.x incompatibility.
t_err_evidence: In step 9, the agent writes a script calling fasttext.cbow(), explicitly acting on the wrong hypothesis formed from reading step 8 output: 'I also see cbow and skipgram functions that are designed to fail, suggesting the user might be using them incorrectly instead of the newer train_unsupervised function.' The actual bug is np.array(probs, copy=False) in predict(), visible in the step 8 output but ignored.
t_commit_evidence: In step 10, the agent runs the cbow script, gets the deprecation exception, and treats this as confirming its wrong hypothesis. From this point the agent is locked into the wrong fix direction (replacing deprecated API calls rather than patching np.array(copy=False)), and never reconsiders the actual NumPy 2.x incompatibility.
trigger_explanation: The agent read the full FastText.py source in step 8, which clearly shows 'np.array(probs, copy=False)' in predict() (the NumPy 2.x-incompatible line), but instead of identifying that as the bug, the agent focused on the deprecated cbow/skipgram/supervised stubs at the bottom of the file and concluded the user was using an outdated API. The agent misinterpreted which part of the file represented the actual problem.
forewarning_evidence: Steps 3 and 6 show fasttext working correctly with get_word_vector() and train_unsupervised/load_model. The agent even notes in step 4: 'This is odd. My fasttext script worked, so the installation is fine, contradicting the user's report' — a direct signal that it was not testing the right code path. The agent should have tested predict() to reproduce the actual failure.
